content: Functional gastrointestinal disorders (FGIDs) encompass a variety of idiopathic conditions that affect different regions of the gastrointestinal tract. These disorders are not caused by structural abnormalities or biochemical dysfunctions but are instead characterized by chronic symptoms that cannot be explained by conventional diagnostic methods. The classification of FGIDs has been standardized through the Rome process, which has undergone several iterations, including Rome I, Rome II, and Rome III. These meetings have established a consensus-based framework for defining and categorizing these disorders, as recommended by the Rome Coordinating Committee. Functional Esophageal Disorders: 1. Functional Heartburn: This condition involves a burning sensation in the chest or throat that is not associated with acid reflux or any identifiable structural abnormalities in the esophagus. 2. Functional Chest Pain of Presumed Esophageal Origin: This refers to non-cardiac chest pain that is thought to originate from the esophagus but lacks any structural or motility-related cause. 3. Functional Dysphagia: This is characterized by difficulty swallowing without any detectable structural or neurological abnormalities. 4. Globus Pharyngis: This condition involves the persistent sensation of a lump or foreign body in the throat, despite the absence of any physical obstruction. Functional Colonic Disorders: 1. Functional Constipation: This is defined by chronic difficulty in passing stools, often accompanied by straining, hard stools, or a sensation of incomplete evacuation, without any identifiable structural or biochemical cause. 2. Functional Rectal Pain: This condition involves recurrent or chronic pain in the rectal area that cannot be attributed to any structural abnormalities. Other Functional Gastrointestinal Disorders: 1. Functional Dyspepsia: This refers to chronic or recurrent pain or discomfort in the upper abdomen, often associated with bloating, nausea, or early satiety, without any identifiable organic cause. 2. Noncardiac Chest Pain: This is chest pain that mimics cardiac pain but is not related to heart disease or any structural abnormalities. 3. Chronic Functional Abdominal Pain: This condition involves persistent or recurrent abdominal pain that is not associated with any structural or biochemical abnormalities. 4. Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS): IBS is characterized by a combination of abdominal pain or discomfort and altered bowel habits (diarrhea, constipation, or both) in the absence of any structural or biochemical explanation. Epidemiology: Functional gastrointestinal disorders are highly prevalent, affecting approximately 60-70% of the populations in both Canada and the United States.
